text:
Ryan Strome is 33, on his fifth NHL team, and past 500 career points, which he reached before this season started. In Calgary he's a middle-six center on 14 minutes a night with seven points in 20 games, and that's about where you'd expect a veteran of his profile to land.

The interesting part is the gap between his chances and his results. The Flames have scored 5.3 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which is the biggest reason his points look thin. He's shooting 7.1% against a usual 12 or so, and the five-on-five play with him is even, 50% of the expected goals. That kind of drought tends to swing back.

He isn't a burner: bottom-20% top speed, a soft shot, and in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season he carried the puck in on only 31% of his entries, so his line lives on dump-ins and the forecheck. He shoots a lot but often from outside. Watch whether he gets to the slot more. If he does, the points should follow.
